newsitem.title: BULGARIA: RUSSIA LOOKS FOR SOFIA CONCESSION TO JOINT GAS FIRM.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA LOOKS FOR SOFIA CONCESSION TO JOINT GAS FIRM.

text.p: Russia is still waiting for Bulgaria's delayed decision on granting a concession to a Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company, Topenergy, Russia's ambassador in Sofia said.
"We are expecting not only Bulgaria's agreement in principle to grant a concession to Topenergy, but its (Bulgaria's) concrete options," Alexander Avdeev said, quoted by local media on Friday.
"The concession should make the gas pipelines profitable. This has not been made so far," Avdeev said.
Topenergy, which was established by Russian gas giant Gazprom and Bulgarian gas monopoly Bulgargas in 1995, is planning to sell and deliver Russian gas to the Balkans via Bulgaria.
In mid-July the Bulgarian cabinet decided to open a procedure for granting a concession to Topenergy.

Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov said a report of a working group which was set up to consider Topenergy's concession would not be ready on October 15 as scheduled but would be delayed by up to several weeks.
The company was at odds with Bulgaria's socialist government earlier this year when the cabinet insisted on stronger state participation and control of the venture.
Currently Gazprom holds 50 percent. The remaining half is distributed among Bulgarian participants, including Bulgargas which holds 25.1 percent.
Avdeev said the Russian side would not change its plans for the project after the murder of Bulgaria's ex-premier and one of Topenergy's founders Andrei Lukanov.
The company has dropped Lukanov as board chairman in a move designed to improve its troubled relations with the Bulgarian government.
"The project is very important for both sides. Work is progressing, but very slowly," he said.
"By politicizing, some people are trying to create tension in our relations," he added.
